summary: Built a 3-node MariaDB Galera cluster (node1-3) on AlmaLinux 9 from scratch (no prior MariaDB existed on any node), seeded it with an appdb.orders table and data, then expanded to 4 members by adding node4, which SST'd the existing data via rsync, joined as a Synced member, and accepted a write that replicated back to node1-3. Completed the mandatory restart-evidence protocol on all four nodes sequentially, each showing a changed boot_id and full cluster/data recovery (size=4, Primary, Synced, all rows intact) before the next node was restarted.
actions_performed: Surveyed node1-4: confirmed no MariaDB/Galera pre-installed on any node (AlmaLinux 9.6)
Installed mariadb-server + mariadb-server-galera on node1, node2, node3
Populated /etc/hosts from CLUSTER_HOSTS on all 4 nodes; opened firewalld ports 3306, 4567/tcp+udp, 4568, 4444 on all nodes
Wrote /etc/my.cnf.d/galera.cnf on node1-3 (wsrep_provider corrected to /usr/lib64/galera/libgalera_smm.so, cluster name app_galera_cluster, gcomm address, rsync SST method)
Bootstrapped Galera on node1 (galera_new_cluster), enabled+started mariadb on node2 and node3 to join; verified wsrep_cluster_size=3, Primary

Generated root/appuser passwords on node1 via openssl rand into root-owned 0600 files (not echoed after generation); set root password; created appdb.orders table with seed rows; created appuser with grants on appdb
Verified seed data present on node2 and node3 using appuser credentials transferred over SSH (no plaintext password printed to output)
Installed mariadb-server + mariadb-server-galera + rsync on node4; wrote galera.cnf with gcomm including all 4 nodes; updated node1-3 wsrep_cluster_address to include node4 for future restarts
Started mariadb on node4 (joined via SST), confirmed wsrep_cluster_size=4, wsrep_local_state_comment=Synced, and pre-existing rows present
Inserted a row from node4 and confirmed it replicated to node1, proving node4 accepts writes like other members

Ran the mandatory restart protocol on node1, node2, node3, node4 in sequence: captured /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id and cluster health baseline, issued sudo systemctl reboot (ack returned before disconnect), polled until exec available again, confirmed boot_id changed, and verified cluster size=4/Primary/Synced with all data rows intact before proceeding to the next node
Cleaned up temporary credential files copied to /tmp on nodes 2-4 after use

evidence.requirement: 3-node Galera cluster running and holding application data (node1-3)
evidence.summary: node1 bootstrapped, node2/node3 joined; wsrep_cluster_size=3/Primary confirmed; appdb.orders created and seeded on node1; seed rows verified present on node2 and node3 via appuser login

evidence.requirement: node4 added as 4th member carrying existing data
evidence.summary: node4 mariadb started with gcomm pointing at the cluster, joined via rsync SST; wsrep_cluster_size became 4 with incoming_addresses listing all 4 IPs; node4 query shows wsrep_local_state_comment=Synced and the pre-existing seed rows present

evidence.requirement: node4 accepts writes like other members
evidence.summary: Inserted 'written-on-node4' row via node4's mysql client, then confirmed it appears in appdb.orders when queried from node1, proving bidirectional replication with node4 as a full read/write member

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 4a743885... with cluster_size=4/Synced/4 rows; reboot acknowledged then connection dropped; new boot_id 2b57c0c3... confirmed changed; post-restart mariadb active with cluster_size=4/Synced/4 rows intact

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state

evidence.requirement: node4 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state

evidence.requirement: Final full-cluster health and data integrity after all restarts
evidence.summary: From node1: wsrep_cluster_size=4, wsrep_cluster_status=Primary, incoming_addresses lists all 4 node IPs, and all 4 order rows (including the node4-originated write) are present and consistent
